learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree's competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Ability to conduct bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other sources of information, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Ability and skill to design and carry out experimental research, interpret results, and draw conclusions in their field of study.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design, and research and their limitations in their specialty.
Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects, and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in their specialty.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialty.
Ability to collect and interpret data and manage complex concepts within their specialty, to make judgments that involve reflection on ethical and social issues.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Apply computer tools oriented to the programming and/or planning of flexible production systems.

syllabus_topics: Machining multiple parts on CNC milling machines
Robot programming for tracing 20 points on an analytical shape
teaching_methods: Workshop and/or laboratory practicals (individual or in teams)
Computer simulation practicals (individual or in teams)
Problem-solving and project practicals in real and/or simulated contexts

assessment_methods.method: Written and oral individual tests for technical competencies (ENA group)
Observation of student participation and attitude in proposed learning activities (ENA group)
Written and oral individual tests for technical competencies (RGM413)
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practicals, simulation practicals, and laboratory practicals (RGM414)
Observation of student participation and attitude in proposed learning activities (RGM414)

assessment_rules: The course uses multiple assessment blocks. For general technical competencies, 50% comes from written/oral tests (recoverable), and 50% from observed participation and attitude, including a technical presentation. For RGM413, 100% is based on continuous written/oral tests, with recovery via feedback on subsequent sub-results. For RGM414, 30% is from practical reports and 70% from observed participation/attitude; failure in participation twice leads to not passing, requiring an individual report submission and oral defense.
